ARC Query Spotlight
Projects by Owning Department

Before You Start
What does this query actually tell you?
This query shows you all projects that exist in your department — every project ID, team member, and start & end date, in one export.
Step-by-Step
How to Run the Query
1
Go to ARC
Navigate to my.columbia.edu and select ARC from the top navigation. Click "Go to ARC" from the ARC Portal homepage.
📍 my.columbia.edu/content/welcome-arc-portal
2
Go to Reporting and Monitoring
From the ARC homepage, select Reporting and Monitoring from the main menu tiles.
📍 ARC Homepage — Select "Reporting and Monitoring"
3
Query Viewer Home Page
In the left-hand navigation, click Query Viewer. Search for queries by name, or leave blank and click Search to see all available queries.
Reporting and Monitoring→Query Viewer
📍 Query Viewer — Search by Query Name
4
Select Query from Dropdown
Expand Chartfield Queries in the left sidebar. Select GL — Projects by Owning Dept.
Chartfield Queries→GL - Projects by Owning Dept
📍 Chartfield Queries → GL - Projects by Owning Dept
Query System Name
The full query name is CU_GL_PROJ_BY_OWN_DEPT_WT_TEAM. See the Naming Convention section below to understand how this is structured.
5
Enter Department Node
Enter your Department Node number. Click the 🔍 magnifying glass to look up by Tree Node. Set Project Status (A = Active, I = Inactive, blank = all). Click View Results.
📍 Enter Dept Node — Use 🔍 to look up your Tree Node
Tip
Leave Project Status blank to return all projects. Type the first few digits of your dept code in the lookup and click Look Up to find your node.
6
Run to Excel
After results appear, click "Excel SpreadSheet" to export the full dataset. CSV and XML formats also available.
Download results in:→Excel SpreadSheet
📍 Results View — Click "Excel SpreadSheet" to export
What You Get
Export includes: Department, Unit, Project ID & Description, Team Role, Team Member, Status, CTV, ARRA, CFDA, Clinical Trial, Sponsor, Funding Mechanism, Award Fund, Billing Frequency, Award Start/End Dates, Purpose Code, Gift Number, Function, and MOT Segment.
ARC Standards
Query Naming Convention
All ARC queries follow a standardized naming structure. Understanding the convention helps you instantly identify what a query does, which module it belongs to, and what filters or output type it produces.
PartDescriptionExample
1Query names should always begin with 'CU'CU
2Identifies the owning moduleGL, KK, PC, AP, PO
3Brief description of what the query returnsJOURNALS, PROJ_BY_OWN_DEPT
4Describes any filters or sorts in the queryBY_DATE, OPRID
5Identifies the type of transaction the query returnsRECONCILIATION, ALLOCATION, WT_TEAM

Output Type
Reads as: "Columbia University · General Ledger · Projects by owning department · with team member data."
Use Queries When: You need to pull the same data set repeatedly without re-entering criteria. For large-scale analysis or cross-module reporting, consider FDS (Financial Data Store) or Advanced ARC Reporting instead.
